name: Humphrey's Peak Trail
text: [approach] The trail starts at the far end of the large gravel lot at the Arizona Snowbowl, off the Snowbowl Road, and passes beneath a chairlift before crossing a meadow.
[descent_text] Go back down the way you came, the Humphreys Trail to the saddle and then the switchbacks to the Snowbowl lot.
[descent_text] Where snow lies on the upper mountain, an ice axe and traction are useful.
earlierWhy: The text only says axe and traction are useful where snow lies, and the web search budget ran out before I could check the line.

name: Ears Between
text: [approach] From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground and head for the foot of the wall, following faint paths through boulders and past what is left of the Crescent Glacier.
earlierWhy: The approach follows boulder paths past what is left of the Crescent Glacier, so no glacier is crossed.

name: Eternal Darkness
text: [overview] Descent: four 60 m rappels, starting slightly skiers left of the summit, reach a snow and dirt gully;
[descent_text] Further rappels lead into the snow and dirt gully, which can be walked down and circled back under the face to the start.
earlierWhy: The text only mentions a snow and dirt gully on the descent, and I could not search further. | no/unsure: The Mountain Project area page puts this 5.10d line on granite walls reached by an easy trail in Cathedral Park, and a club wiki says the park avoids glacier travel; snow is only a warning about slopes.

name: Standard route

name: Standard route
earlierWhy: No route text and no verified facts about this line. | no/unsure: A trip report has the party going up the east bowl on rock to a class 4 summit block with no ice or glacier travel.

name: Standard route
earlierWhy: No route text and no verified facts about this line. | no/unsure: A trip report describes talus, a loose pass chute and a class 3-4 rock arete to the summit, with no glacier on the line.

name: Direct South Face
text: [descent_text] Beyond the saddle, sand or snow leads to the dirt road running along the creek's north bank, and you ford the creek at the point opposite your car.
earlierWhy: Summer rock routes; sand or snow only on the low saddle descent and no glacier on Lone Pine Peak.

name: Land of Little Rain
text: [descent_text] From the saddle, sand or snow leads to the dirt road along the creek's north bank.
earlierWhy: Summer rock routes; sand or snow only on the low saddle descent and no glacier on Lone Pine Peak.

name: Standard route

name: Standard route

name: Northeast Face
text: [detailed_rack] Standard rack with some long slings, since the line wanders, plus an ice axe.
earlierWhy: No glacier on this rock face; only an ice axe is mentioned, so snow is unclear.

name: Ok Balto, hike!
text: [overview] The dihedral on the back side of the neighboring route, with glacier-polished gray rock on the part of the corner that faces left.
earlierWhy: Glacier only describes polished rock; no snow evidence.

name: Planaria
text: [approach] Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake.
earlierWhy: Glacier is only in the trailhead name; Temple Crag rock line, snow not settled.

name: Quickly Without Asking (Tallac Headwall Direct)
text: [what_to_bring] ice axes and perhaps crampons — getting to the wall base
earlierWhy: Snow may affect the start only; no glacier at Tallac.

name: South Ridge
text: [what_to_bring] ice axe — may be needed, depending on snowpack
earlierWhy: Axe may be needed depending on snowpack; peak not verified. | no/unsure: The area page places the peak above Blue Lake, reached by trail from Lake Sabrina, as a short 5.6 rock ridge with no glacier or snow mentioned.

name: Angels and Demons
text: [approach] The wall is reached either from Mineral King via Monarch Lake and over Glacier Pass, or by crossing Timber Gap and following Cliff Creek up to Spring Lake.
earlierWhy: Glacier Pass is only a place name on the approach.

name: The Speed of Life
text: [overview] From the dam, cross over and hike a steep, loose hillside to the bottom-most tongue of the rock, often guarded by an ice or snow patch;
earlierWhy: Base is often guarded by an ice or snow patch; no glacier.

name: Thunder Col and East Ridge
earlierWhy: No text; Class 4 line not verified.

name: 2nd Apron Left Side
text: [overview] Start on angling cracks by the snow tongue, trend left under a little roof, then work through 500-600 ft of fractured rock at 5.6, some 5.7, to a grassy terrace.
earlierWhy: No glacier on this Mt Blue Sky face; the snow tongue at the start may persist.
